$comment: Wire protocols the dispatcher can speak. `handler` names the Provider subclass in lib/dispatch/provider.py - the registry resolves it from this table, so adding a transport is a data edit plus one class. `capability_ceiling` is the physical limit of the protocol: a raw completion endpoint cannot read a disk regardless of what an operator types into the channel record.

data.label: Claude CLI
data.description: Local `claude --print` subprocess. Full agentic harness: the CLI owns tool execution, filesystem access, and its own permission sandbox. Prompts leave the host for Anthropic.

data.label: Ollama Native
data.description: Ollama's own /api/generate. Single-shot prompt in, completion out, with a first-class system field. No harness: the response is text and nothing else runs.

data.label: OpenAI-Compatible Chat
data.description: The /v1/chat/completions lingua franca - Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, OpenRouter, and the commercial APIs all answer here. Tool calls are in the protocol; the agency harness (lib/dispatch/harness) executes them, so the ceiling extends exactly as far as the executor implements: filesystem_read, not write or shell.

data.label: Ollama Chat
data.description: Ollama's own /api/chat: message history plus function declarations. The model emits structured tool calls and the agency harness (lib/dispatch/harness) executes them under mission policy. The ceiling extends exactly as far as the executor implements: filesystem_read, not write or shell. Tasks offered no function take a single text turn.
